svg.title: Self-attention as matrix multiplies, from embedding lookup through the output, row 2 highlighted.
svg.text: Self-attention as matrix multiplies — from token IDs to output
Same math as the step-by-step version, batched over all six tokens. Row 2 (highlighted) = the z⁽²⁾ from before.
⓪ Embedding lookup: X = OneHot · E
E is the learned embedding table. A one-hot row selects one row of E; stacking six one-hots gives X.
Toy vocab of 7 shown; a real table has ~50,000 rows. (Row 2 = journey → picks E’s journey row = x⁽²⁾.)
① Project every token at once: Q = X·W_q, K = X·W_k, V = X·W_v
Each output row is x⁽ⁱ⁾·W — the same projection done to all six tokens in one matmul, not six.
② All query·key scores at once: S = Q·Kᵀ / √dₖ (6×6)
Q(6×2)·Kᵀ(2×6) = S(6×6). Cell (i,j) = query i (row) scored against key j (column).
Kᵀ = K with rows and columns swapped (T = transpose): the 6×2 becomes 2×6.
We transpose so the shared dim (2) lines up, so each query row can dot each key column.
Row 2 = [0.31 0.52 0.52 0.29 0.28 0.36] — the six ω₂ᵢ scores from v4 Step 3.
Softmax each row on its own → every row is positive and sums to 1. Row 2 = the attention weights α₂ᵢ.
④ Weighted sum of values: Z = A·V (6×2)
A(6×6)·V(6×2) = Z(6×2). Each row = that token’s weights times V — all six context vectors at once.
Row 2 = z⁽²⁾ = [0.36 0.60] — exactly the running-total result you built in the v4 loop.

g.text: Heads-up: with these toy 3-dim embeddings (dₖ=2), the six output rows come out nearly identical — attention is
almost uniform here. With real, meaningful embeddings the weights sharpen and the rows genuinely diverge.

svg.text: Like your MNIST net: per-neuron loops collapse into one matmul — same idea as X·W, Q·Kᵀ, and A·V here.

g.text: Make X 3-D — each slice is another 6-word sequence (e.g. 4×6×3 = 4 slices).
Projections: flatten to 24×3, multiply by the shared W_q, W_k, W_v, then reshape the 24×2 outputs
back into four separate 6×2 Q, K, V slices.
Each slice then runs Steps ②–④ on its own — all four at once, in parallel on the GPU.
